thread.title: Apple, 3M Lead Nasdaq, Dow Lower; This Bank Stock Breaks Out

author: EdJenner
title: Apple, 3M Lead Nasdaq, Dow Lower; This Bank Stock Breaks Out
text:
The Nasdaq paced modest early losses in stocks today , but the market showed a bit of strength after the first half-hour of trading. Banking play Popular ( BPOP ) staged a breakout.
X
The tech composite is down just 0.2% after dropping more than 0.5% early. The leading index is on pace for a fourth mild decline in a row.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 0.2% as 3M ( MMM ) and Apple ( AAPL ) each lost 1 point or more. The S&P 500 erased mild losses to hover near the break-even level.
Apple remains in good shape as the iPhone, MacBook and digital services giant continues to tread on the north side of its rising 50-day moving average. The stock is up 6% past a 179.04 double-bottom buy point , and thus is outside the proper buy zone of 5% .
The S&P SmallCap 600 dropped 0.4%.
Toymakers helped lead the market upside. Hasbro ( HAS ) rose more than 12% following Q2 results. The company’s earnings fell 8% to 48 cents a share, much higher than expected. Sales fell 7%, posting a smaller year-over-year decline than a 16% drop in Q1.
Some banks defied the decline. Puerto Rico-focused Popular ( BPOP ), the holding company of Banco Popular de Puerto Rico, rallied more than 2%, to 49.15, and cleared a 48.27 proper buy point in a five-week flat base .
Popular posted a 27% jump in earnings to $1.19 a share, marking the biggest increase in nearly three years. Revenue soared 31% to $715.7 million.
Popular’s relative strength line is not quite yet at a new high but is angling sharply higher, a good sign.
Popular carries a lackluster 69 Composite Rating from IBD, as seen in Stock Checkup , but that masks a healthy 85 Relative Price Strength Rating.
Chip and data storage-related firms suffered some of the morning’s heavy selling.
Micron Technology ( MU ), an expert in flash storage drives, gapped down at the open and sank more than 4% to 52.65 in heavy turnover.
The big-cap member of IBD’s Computer-Data Storage industry group has been in basing mode since reversing off a 64.66 high on May 30. Back then, Micron was trying to move past a 63.52 cup-base buy point but backtracked quickly after a May 29 breakout attempt.
The cup featured no handle and had elements of a double bottom . However, as seen on the accompanying daily chart, the middle interim peak of 54.27 was lodged in the lower half of the base, a no-no.
Overseas, the Shanghai Composite rallied 1.1% overnight to 2859, extending its gain from a July 6 low of 2691 to 6.2%. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng bench mark edged 0.1% higher.
Among Chinese ADRs and ADSs, social network Momo ( MOMO ) pulled back lightly after rebounding 3.4% last week. The stock is trying to hold buying support near its 10-week moving average and is also in Week 6 of a potential new base.
Momo is a member of IBD Sector Leaders . The computer-generated screen of high-growth stocks through Friday has generated a price-weighted year-to-date return of 22.3% since Jan. 1, vs. 4.3% for the S&P 500.
In other markets, WTI crude oil futures jumped 1% to $68.92 a barrel to improve a year-to-date gain to 14%.
The yield on the bench mark U.S. Treasury 10-year bond continues to edge higher and is now at 2.89%, reaching a one-month high.
